structure.title: Topics as starting points
structure.text: Essays begin from a custom, quotation, memory, or question, then follow associations that may alter the original subject.

structure.title: A self under revision
structure.text: Across the collection, changing judgments and bodily experience keep testing borrowed wisdom. Individual essays can be read separately without becoming isolated verdicts.

people.name: Montaigne
people.text: A retired French magistrate who shut himself in his tower library to write about himself, and found that the subject changed every time he looked.

people.name: Custom
people.text: Montaigne's theme that much of what we take for nature or reason is only the habit of our own country and time.

people.name: Judgment
people.text: His practice of trying out his judgement on any subject, from cannibals to thumbs, to see how it holds up rather than to reach a verdict.

context.title: An essay as an attempt
context.text: The form permits revision, digression, and uncertainty. An apparent departure may be the means by which an assumption is tested.
context.takeaway: Follow movement rather than demand a final doctrine.

context.title: Ancient companions
context.text: Quotations supply examples and arguments, but Montaigne often tests them against his own experience. Classical authority does not end the conversation.
context.takeaway: Watch borrowed wisdom meet a living body.

notice.why: Honesty about variation becomes part of the inquiry.

notice.text: Follow small details of habit and sensation.
notice.why: General claims are repeatedly returned to particular life.

opening: Montaigne sits down to write about friendship, fear, education, or some odd thing he has read, and sooner or later finds himself implicated. His memory fails, his body interrupts, and his behaviour refuses to match the dignity of his opinions. The essays have the freedom of a conversation with someone too curious to keep up a flawless appearance. A minor observation can lead into a major uncertainty, and the writer's willingness to revise himself makes his company more trustworthy than a performance of certainty would be.
